issues.legal_issue: A detailed eyewitness report may be treated as the first information report when earlier information was only unrecorded village gossip and no investigation had begun on its basis.
material_facts: A village official had heard a report based on village talk that the deceased had been attacked, but the source was not an eyewitness and had not named all the accused.

Before any investigation began on that information, an eyewitness gave a detailed statement naming the accused and describing their participation; it was recorded and signed, and the authorities acted on it.
issues.conclusion: The detailed eyewitness statement was properly treated as the first information report and admitted in evidence; the earlier village report did not make it inadmissible.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 154 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, the court considered whether information had been recorded as the formal report and whether investigation had begun on the earlier information. Receipt and recording of a report is not a condition precedent to setting an investigation in motion, but the earlier, unrecorded village gossip in this case had not started an investigation. No earlier case is cited for this ruling.

rule.if: criminal_case and earlier_information_is_unverified_gossip and earlier_information_not_formally_recorded and investigation_not_started_on_earlier_information and later_detailed_eyewitness_statement_recorded_before_investigation

predicates.criminal_case: The matter is a criminal prosecution concerning an alleged offence.
predicates.earlier_information_is_unverified_gossip: An official received an account based on general talk rather than an informant's personal knowledge.
predicates.earlier_information_not_formally_recorde: The earlier account was not recorded as a formal report of the offence.
predicates.investigation_not_started_on_earlier_inf: The authorities had not begun investigating on the basis of the earlier account.
predicates.later_detailed_eyewitness_statement_reco: An eyewitness later gave a detailed account that was recorded before investigation began.

issues.definition: When a criminal case involves only unverified, unrecorded earlier gossip and no investigation has begun on it, a later recorded, detailed eyewitness account may be treated as the first information.

issues.legal_issue: Failure to call a witness whose information came only from village talk does not require an adverse inference when that witness had no personal knowledge of the occurrence.
material_facts: The prosecution did not call the village official who had relayed the earlier report.
That official's information came from village talk, and he was not an eyewitness; his evidence could not have supplied a firsthand account of the attack.
issues.conclusion: The failure to call the village official did not justify an adverse inference against the prosecution.
issues.legal_principle: The Court reasoned that a witness without personal knowledge could not have unfolded the prosecution account, and that the witness's repetition of village talk would have had little corroborative value. No statutory provision or earlier case is cited for this ruling.

predicates.criminal_prosecution: The matter is a prosecution for a criminal offence.
predicates.absent_witness_had_no_personal_knowledge: A witness who was not called had no firsthand knowledge of the event being tried.
predicates.absent_witness_knew_only_unverified_rumo: The absent witness's account came only from unverified talk by others.

issues.definition: When a prosecution does not call a witness who had no firsthand knowledge and knew the event only through rumor, the omission does not warrant an adverse inference.

issues.legal_issue: Omission of eyewitnesses' names from an inquest report does not by itself discredit their testimony when the evidence shows that they were examined and the circumstances explain the omission.
material_facts: The investigating officer prepared an inquest report that named one eyewitness but omitted the names of two other claimed eyewitnesses.
The officer said that naming the one witness accorded with the practice, and the two omitted witnesses testified that the officer had examined them.
The earlier detailed report already named the two witnesses, and the challenge based on their omission from the inquest report had not been raised in the trial court or the High Court.
issues.conclusion: The omission did not support the claim that the two witnesses were absent or had been added as an afterthought, and their testimony was not discredited on that basis.
issues.legal_principle: The Court assessed the omission in the context of the officer's explanation, the witnesses' evidence that they had been examined, and their prior identification in the report of the occurrence. No statutory provision or earlier case is cited for this ruling.

rule.if: criminal_case and eyewitness_names_omitted_from_inquest and investigating_officer_examined_witnesses and omission_explained_by_recording_practice and witnesses_named_in_earlier_report

predicates.criminal_case: The matter is a criminal prosecution in which eyewitness testimony is relied on.
predicates.eyewitness_names_omitted_from_inquest: An inquest record omits the names of some people who later testify as eyewitnesses.
predicates.investigating_officer_examined_witnesses: The investigating officer and the witnesses give evidence that the officer examined those witnesses.
predicates.omission_explained_by_recording_practice: The officer explains that the omission accords with the practice used when preparing the record.
predicates.witnesses_named_in_earlier_report: The omitted witnesses had already been identified in an earlier report of the occurrence.

issues.definition: When an inquest record omits eyewitnesses' names but the officer examined them, the omission is explained by recording practice, and an earlier report names them, the omission does not discredit their testimony.

issues.legal_issue: Qualified medical opinion that an injury could cause immediate death does not displace eyewitness testimony when the medical evidence does not establish that the victim necessarily died or became unable to move at once.
material_facts: A doctor testified that one head injury could cause immediate death and that a victim who immediately suffered shock and unconsciousness could not run.

On further questioning, the doctor explained that the onset of shock depended on the victim's resistance and that the victim could run if shock had not set in immediately; he did not say that this victim necessarily died at once.
The eyewitnesses testified that the victim moved after being injured and asked for water, and the medical evidence did not unequivocally contradict that account.
issues.conclusion: The medical evidence did not establish that the victim died upon receiving the first injury, and it did not justify rejecting the eyewitness testimony that he moved and spoke afterward.
issues.legal_principle: The Court treated the doctor's evidence as opinion evidence and read the qualified answer together with the doctor's explanation on re-examination and the evidence concerning the victim's condition. It relied on no earlier case for this ruling.

predicates.criminal_appeal: The matter is an appeal against criminal convictions.
predicates.medical_testimony_is_qualified_opinion: The medical witness gives an opinion about what an injury could cause, rather than an unequivocal conclusion about what necessarily occurred.
predicates.doctor_does_not_say_death_or_unconscious: The doctor does not conclude that the victim necessarily died or became unconscious immediately after the injury.
predicates.eyewitnesses_describe_post_injury_moveme: Eyewitnesses describe the victim moving or speaking after the injury.

issues.definition: In a criminal appeal, qualified medical opinion that does not establish inevitable immediate death or unconsciousness does not displace eyewitness testimony describing post-injury movement.

issues.legal_issue: Imprecise estimates and peripheral discrepancies about an occurrence do not invalidate eyewitness testimony when the discrepancies are compatible with the record and do not materially undermine the account.
material_facts: The challenges concerned the witnesses' estimates of when the men had eaten and when the attack occurred, the distance the victim ran, the absence of a visible blood streak when the investigating officer arrived, and the failure to seize the vessel used to bring water.

The High Court and Supreme Court considered the timing and distance estimates non-precise recollections; the record showed blood at a distance from the body and blood on the victim's clothing, and the water vessel had no direct connection to the offence.
issues.conclusion: These criticisms did not materially discredit the eyewitness testimony.
issues.legal_principle: The Court assessed estimates in light of ordinary limits on observation and memory, the lapse before testimony, and the corroborating physical evidence; it also held that the investigating officer could leave unrelated material uncollected. No earlier case is cited for this ruling.

predicates.criminal_appeal: The matter is an appeal against criminal convictions.
predicates.eyewitness_testimony_is_supported_by_cor: The eyewitness account is supported by other evidence in the record.
predicates.challenged_details_are_imprecise_or_peri: The challenged matters concern estimates, incidental details, or evidence not directly connected to the offence.
predicates.record_does_not_materially_conflict_with: The remaining record does not materially contradict the eyewitness account.

issues.definition: When corroborated eyewitness testimony is challenged only on imprecise or peripheral details that do not materially conflict with the record, those discrepancies do not discredit the witnesses.

issues.legal_issue: The Supreme Court may examine the record closely in a death-sentence appeal when a serious claim of miscarriage of justice based on medical evidence is raised.
material_facts: The appeal challenged convictions that included death sentences and alleged a grave miscarriage of justice because the medical evidence supposedly conflicted with the eyewitness testimony.
The Supreme Court examined the record and found no support for that alleged conflict.
issues.conclusion: The Court examined the record with anxious care and found no ground to interfere on the asserted basis.
issues.legal_principle: Under Article 136 of the Constitution, the Court does not ordinarily review the record in this manner, but it may examine it with anxious care in a criminal appeal involving a death sentence when a serious claim of miscarriage of justice is raised. No earlier case is cited for this statement.

predicates.appeal_under_special_leave: The matter is a criminal appeal brought by special leave.
predicates.death_sentence_at_issue: A death sentence is under challenge in the appeal.
predicates.serious_miscarriage_claim_based_on_evide: The appellant alleges a grave miscarriage of justice based on an asserted evidentiary conflict.

issues.definition: When a special-leave criminal appeal places a death sentence at issue and raises a serious evidentiary claim of miscarriage, the Court may examine the record with anxious care.

issues.legal_issue: A death sentence is justified when the accused are proved to have inflicted the fatal injuries in a brutal and callous murder.
material_facts: Medical evidence established that two injuries were necessarily fatal.
The courts accepted the evidence identifying two accused as the authors of those fatal injuries.
The Court described the murder as brutal and callous and noted that the death sentences were imposed only on the two accused who inflicted the fatal injuries.
issues.conclusion: The death sentences were justified, and the Court rejected the challenge to sentence.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied Section 302 of the Indian Penal Code and held that the sentences were justified without resort to Section 34. It explained that Section 34 concerns constructive liability for persons acting with a common intention and noted that the other participants had not received the extreme penalty. Although the appellant cited decisions, the supplied judgment does not identify them or rely on a particular earlier case for this ruling.

rule.if: appeal_challenging_death_sentence and accused_individually_attributed_fatal_injuries and fatal_nature_of_injuries_established and murder_found_brutal_and_callous

predicates.appeal_challenging_death_sentence: The matter is an appeal challenging a death sentence for murder.
predicates.accused_individually_attributed_fatal_in: The evidence accepted by the court identifies the accused as the persons who inflicted the fatal injuries.
predicates.fatal_nature_of_injuries_established: The medical evidence establishes that the injuries inflicted were fatal.
predicates.murder_found_brutal_and_callous: The court finds the murder brutal and callous.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges a death sentence and the accused are proved to have inflicted medically established fatal injuries in a murder found brutal and callous, the sentence is justified.
